citations.quote:
Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

derivations.claim: Extend the symmetric binomial to integer top indices using its finite product in the generic variable. If $d\ge1$ and $s\ge0$, negating every numerator quantum integer gives $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}-d\\s\end{smallmatrix}\right]_v=(-1)^s\left[\begin{smallmatrix}d+s-1\\s\end{smallmatrix}\right]_v$. The right side is a Laurent polynomial by [F2], so this equality defines its integral specialization without dividing a specialized factorial. Put $g_d(s)=\left[\begin{smallmatrix}d+s-1\\d-1\end{smallmatrix}\right]_v$; symmetry makes the negative binomial $(-1)^sg_d(s)$, and $g_d(0)=1$.

Establish an exact recurrence for this sequence. For an indeterminate $Q$, let $G_{n,k}(Q)$ be the ordinary Gaussian polynomial, characterized by $G_{n,k}(v^2)=v^{k(n-k)}\left[\begin{smallmatrix}n\\k\end{smallmatrix}\right]_v$. Both Pascal recurrences in [F2] give $G_{n,k}=G_{n-1,k-1}+Q^kG_{n-1,k}$, with out-of-range terms zero. Put $h_d(s)=G_{d+s-1,d-1}$ and $h_d(-1)=0$. Thus $h_1(s)=1$ and $h_{d+1}(s)=h_d(s)+Q^dh_{d+1}(s-1)$ for $s\ge0$. Multiplying formal series coefficientwise yields $\sum_{s\ge0}h_d(s)t^s=\prod_{j=0}^{d-1}(1-Q^jt)^{-1}$ by induction on $d$. Each inverse here is the formal geometric series, so no coefficient-ring element is divided. Substitution $Q=v^2$ and $t\mapsto v^{-(d-1)}t$ gives $$\sum_{s\ge0}g_d(s)t^s=\prod_{j=0}^{d-1}(1-v^{2j-d+1}t)^{-1}.$$ Writing the denominator as $\sum_{j=0}^dp_jt^j$, its constant term is $p_0=1$ and its top coefficient is $p_d=(-1)^dv^{\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}(2j-d+1)}=(-1)^d$. Coefficient comparison therefore gives $\sum_{j=0}^dp_jg_d(n-j)=0$ for every $n\ge d$, with a unit coefficient on the oldest term.

A zero tail forces a zero initial coefficient over every ring. More precisely, if $z$ belongs to any $R$-module and $g_d(s)z=0$ for every $s\ge S$, first use the recurrence of step 2.1 at $n=S+d-1$ to obtain $p_dg_d(S-1)z=0$ when $S>0$. The other $d$ terms have indices at least $S$ and are zero. Since $p_d=(-1)^d$ is a unit, $g_d(S-1)z=0$. Repeat this finite backward argument until $g_d(0)z=z=0$. If $S=0$ the conclusion already follows from $g_d(0)=1$. This argument never divides a quantum integer or assumes that a nonzero scalar acts injectively.

Fix $i$ and $a>m_i$, put $d=a-m_i>0$ and $z=F_i^{(a)}x$. The only surviving term of the rank-one reordering of $E_i^{(s)}F_i^{(a+s)}x$ has contraction index $s$, since every other term ends in a positive divided power killing $x$. Its toral factor acts on $x$ by $\left[\begin{smallmatrix}m_i-a\\s\end{smallmatrix}\right]_v$, so [F1] and step 1.1 give $$E_i^{(s)}F_i^{(a+s)}x=(-1)^sg_d(s)z.$$ For all $s\ge S:=\max(0,\lambda_i-a+1)$, the putative composition label of $F_i^{(a+s)}x$ has $i$th coordinate $\lambda_i-a-s<0$, hence this vector is zero by the given support. Thus $g_d(s)z=0$ for every $s\ge S$. Step 3.1 proves $F_i^{(a)}x=z=0$. This establishes every required divided relation independently, including $a$ larger than the characteristic or quantum characteristic.

If $X=U_Rx$, triangular spanning in [F1] and the highest conditions give $X=U_R^-x$: positive nonconstant terms kill $x$ and the middle toral terms evaluate by its character. The negative-half map $y\mapsto yx$ is onto, and step 4.1 makes each generator $F_i^{(a)}$, $a>m_i$, of the displayed left ideal vanish at $x$. It therefore factors through exactly the stated negative quotient. This is a concrete quotient construction over $R$, rather than a specialization of a generic surjectivity claim.

Suppose the quotient is supplied with the highest-module action described in the Statement. The map of step 5.1 commutes with negative divided powers by construction and with all toral elements by homogeneous degrees and the integer-weight characters. For a positive divided generator acting on a negative word, apply the same finite integral reordering identity in the quotient and in $X$; move the toral coefficients to the highest line and kill the positive tails. Each resulting negative term has the same coefficient and the same image in the two modules. Linearity proves commutation with every positive divided generator, hence with all of $U_R$. Any such map is determined by its highest vector because the quotient is generated by the negative words. At $N=1$ there are no simple-root relations and the same argument gives the rank-one cyclic quotient directly; the zero module and $r=0$ are included. All scalar operations in the relation proof were Laurent-polynomial identities and multiplication by the units $(-1)^d$, so no flatness or Choice hypothesis is required.

boundaries.evidence: Step 6.1 includes r=0 with the same support and highest argument.
Step 6.1 includes the zero module and arbitrary coefficient rings.
Step 6.1 treats N=1 with no simple-root relations.
Steps 2.1–4.1 use Laurent-polynomial identities and oldest coefficient ±1 even with torsion, zero divisors or vanished factorials.
Step 4.1 proves each a>m separately, including equal adjacent parts; it does not infer divided relations from an ordinary power.
Steps 2.1–6.1 use finite recurrences and word rewriting, making no basis selection, vector-space splitting or Choice use.

risk_review.notes: Constructed local proof; no independent mathematical acceptance or gate closure is claimed.
